subject: How can I add spatial correlation to designed matrix (Z) model?

messages.author: 752a2e6de073e297
messages.subject: How can I add spatial correlation to designed matrix (Z) model?
parts:
Hello everyone!

I have a model that requires to add spatial correlation to Z model (designed matrix model).

In other words, I have a model y=iid_X + Zu, where Z is a designed matrix. I need to make u not a just a vector of random effects, but also spatially correlated.

I have read a few documents and but couldn't find a direct answer. I really appreciate if someone could advise on this problem.

Thanks!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How can I add spatial correlation to designed matrix (Z) model?
parts:
Normally the f() notation and variants is sufficient, and the Zu is just
to quickly map back to a standard/classical model, not the other way
around.

You may look at the SPDE book at www.r-inla.org and check if you find
something there.

H

parts:
In the SPDE-models we have a kind of Zu term but we name A in place of Z. Thus, as long as an SPDE model for 'u' is fine, you can consider the examples in the SPDE-book.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How can I add spatial correlation to designed matrix (Z) model?
parts:
Yes,
as Elias said, terms of the form A u are used for the SPDE models.  But the system can apply it to any model of any type, so it doesn't matter if u is an spde, or iid, or some other inla-supported model, and setup in the same way with inla.stack().
The general background is included in this paper:
https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v063i19

So if you have a pre-defined Z-matrix and a well defined u-model, then you can just use Z as the A-matrix for the u-effect, as defined in the paper.
Nearly all examples we have are for SPDE models, but there's nothing special about that construction.

Finn
